A common prime \(\ell\ne5\) gives fifth roots \(x\) and \((x+1)/2\), with \(x\) of order five; checking the five powers forces \(\ell=11\) and \(x\equiv5,9\pmod{11}\). For \(\ell=5\) the shared residue is \(x\equiv1\pmod5\). Modulo \(25\), \(F(1+5t)\equiv5\); modulo \(121\), the two possible residue lifts have incompatible linear conditions, so both prime valuations are exactly one. Chinese remainder and multiplicative-order arguments give all gcd classes and least periods, independently corroborated by exact integer arithmetic. The infinite assertion follows from the proof, not the finite computational enumeration.

value.rationale: The fifth term is the first odd-prime-index member of a naturally paired repunit/binomial-transform family at which a non-index common prime appears. The characterization isolates the unique off-index prime \(11\) through rigidity of two affinely related fifth roots, and determines every possible gcd, square-factor obstruction, base period, residue frequency, and \(2^k\)-specialized period. These exact common-divisor data concern simultaneous divisibility of two published integer sequences, not merely a renamed identity or arbitrary finite sample.
